results.title: control: a DDL statement is findable in postgres_logs by its nonce
results.detail: create/drop table -> HTTP 201; the statement text was first seen in postgres_logs 32s after the fire, on a 192s search at a 30s poll interval. The search works and ingestion is live, so a miss below is a miss.

results.title: a bare DELETE on the audit table in postgres_logs
results.detail: delete -> HTTP 201; searched postgres_logs for its nonce across the full 192s window: not found. log_statement=ddl does not cover DML, so the erasure of an audit row is not itself a logged statement.

results.title: a bare TRUNCATE on the audit table in postgres_logs
results.detail: truncate -> HTTP 201; searched across the full 192s window: not found. log_statement groups TRUNCATE under mod with the data-modifying statements, not under ddl, so emptying the table in one statement is unlogged too.

results.title: provenance on a statement the platform ran for you
results.detail: the control line is attributed to role=postgres, application_name=mgmt-api, and the platform appended a provenance comment naming the calling route and the acting identity (3 lines: -- source: POST /v1/projects/:ref/database/query -- user: pat:<id> -- date: 2026-09-08T06:35:20.700Z). Every tenant path - Dashboard, Management API, MCP - arrives as this one database role, so per-person attribution is not in Postgres.

results.title: log_statement through the Management API
results.detail: GET config/database/postgres -> HTTP 200, 1 key(s) (log_connections). log_statement absent. PUT log_statement=mod -> HTTP 400: {"message":": Unrecognized key: \"log_statement\""}. Statement-level DML logging is therefore a pgaudit job, not a config toggle.

results.title: pgaudit session mode catches the delete and the truncate
results.detail: create extension -> true; alter role postgres set pgaudit.log to 'write' -> true (rolconfig now pgaudit.log=write); no restart performed. DELETE -> HTTP 201: AUDIT line first seen 32s later. TRUNCATE -> HTTP 201: AUDIT line first seen 32s later. Both statements ran in sessions opened AFTER the ALTER ROLE, which is what makes a role-level GUC apply without a reboot.
results.evidence:
AUDIT: SESSION,1,1,WRITE,DELETE,,,"delete from auth.audit_log_entries where payload->>'action' = 'a04dellsivcvqs'

-- source: POST /v1/projects/:ref/database/query
-- user: pat:<id>
-- date: 2026-09-08T06:38:37.522Z",<not logged>
AUDIT: SESSION,1,1,WRITE,TRUNCATE TABLE,,,"-- a04trutaq4no0k
truncate table auth.audit_log_entries

-- source: POST /v1/projects/:ref/database/query
-- user: pat:<id>
-- date: 2026-09-08T06:38:37.667Z",<not logged>

results.title: pgaudit object mode: audit this one table, log nothing else
results.detail: auditor role -> true; grant on the audit table -> true; pgaudit.role=a04_auditor -> true; pgaudit.log back to none -> true. DELETE -> HTTP 201: AUDIT line first seen 33s later (AUDIT: OBJECT,1,1,WRITE,DELETE,TABLE,auth.audit_log_entries,"delete from auth.audit_log_en). TRUNCATE -> HTTP 201: AUDIT line absent within the 193s window. Object mode logs only statements touching the granted table, so it adds no lines for the rest of the database traffic.
results.evidence:
AUDIT: OBJECT,1,1,WRITE,DELETE,TABLE,auth.audit_log_entries,"delete from auth.audit_log_entries where payload->>'action' = 'a04obj7s3l8cmq'

-- source: POST /v1/projects/:ref/database/query
-- user: pat:<id>
-- date: 2026-09-08T06:39:11.169Z",<not logged>

results.title: log_connections through the API, and whether the write took
results.detail: PUT log_connections=true -> HTTP 200. GET config/database/postgres now echoes log_connections=true; a session opened after the PUT reports pg_settings log_connections=on. A "connection authorized" line did NOT appear within 97s. The write took.

results.title: revoking the minted login roles, verified with the correct password
results.detail: the same credential answered OK immediately before revocation. DELETE cli/login-role -> HTTP 200 ({"message":"ok"}); 2 role(s) had been minted. Reconnecting afterwards with the SAME correct password: psql: error: connection to server at "<pooler-host>" (<ip>), port 5432 failed: FATAL: (EAUTHQUERY) user not found in the database. Revocation confirmed: the credential worked before the DELETE and not after.
